title: The Berlin Wall in Mitte: Quick Summary
items: **The Wall runs straight through central Berlin,** not just through Bernauer Strasse or the East Side Gallery, but almost nobody notices it.
**What survives in the centre is the trace, not the Wall:** a 1.3 kilometre double row of cobblestones with bronze plaques reading Berliner Mauer 1961 to 1989.
**The line crosses places you already visit:** near the Reichstag and the Spree, at the Brandenburg Gate, at Potsdamer Platz and Checkpoint Charlie.
**The Brandenburg Gate stood in East Berlin but inside the death strip,** unreachable from either side from 1961 to 1989.
**The centre lost its Wall fast** because the land became the most valuable in the city; the cobblestone line was laid later so the course would not be lost.
**For the real thing, go north to Bernauer Strasse,** the one place a full section of the border system still stands.
**My move: pair a short line-spotting walk in Mitte with one proper stop at the Bernauer memorial** for the most honest picture on foot.
